---
title: "Technical details"
---

quartodown generates a [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) website project from the
package sources, so the man pages, vignettes and generated pages are all Quarto
pages, and every Quarto feature works.

## How a build works

`quartodown::build_site()` runs in three stages:

1. **Before rendering**, it installs the package into a temporary library,
   writes a Quarto project into `_quarto/` and runs the reference pages'
   examples against that package.
2. **During rendering**, Quarto renders `_quarto/` into `docs/`, running the
   vignettes against that package.
3. **After rendering**, it links code to its documentation, adds hover tooltips,
   puts the [logo](../customizing.qmd#the-logo) by each page's title and writes
   the [redirect](../customizing.qmd#redirects) pages.

With
[`development: mode: devel`](../customizing.qmd#development-and-release-sites),
the site goes in `docs/dev/` instead, and a build into `docs/` leaves `dev/` as
it is.

In an interactive session it then serves the site with `preview_site()`. The
server keeps running for the rest of the session, so after a rebuild the open
page reloads instead of a new one opening.

`build_site(devel = TRUE)` skips the install and loads the package from source
with `pkgload::load_all()` instead. It is faster, but code that starts other R
processes (for example with callr or parallel) won't find the package, and
build-stage `\Sexpr{}` macros in the man pages don't run.

`build_site()`'s `workers` argument sets the number of processes to build with.
More than one needs the [mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org/) package.

`build_site(freeze = TRUE)` reuses the results of code from an earlier build,
kept in `_quarto/_freeze/`, for pages whose source hasn't changed (Quarto's
[freeze](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html#freeze)).
Committing `_quarto/_freeze/` lets builds on CI reuse them too.

::: {.callout-warning}
Freeze only checks each page's own source, not your package's code or the
packages it uses. After changing a function or updating a dependency, the pages
running that code keep their old output until you delete `_quarto/_freeze/`.
:::

Throughout the build, the environment variable `IN_QUARTODOWN` is `"true"`, so
the package's code can tell it is running for the site, and `IN_QUARTODOWN_PKG`
is the package's name.

`_quarto/` is rewritten on every build, and gitignored by
`quartodown::use_quartodown()`. To change the site, edit `_quartodown/` instead
(see [Customizing your site](../customizing.qmd)).

```text
_quarto/
├── _quarto.yml                   # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.qmd                     # home page
├── reference/
│   ├── index.qmd                 # function reference index
│   └── <topic>.qmd               # a page per man/*.Rd
├── authors.qmd                   # authors and citation page
├── vignettes/                    # the vignettes, as they are
├── man/figures/                  # images for the README and man pages
├── NEWS.md                       # changelog, titled, with issues and users linked
├── _quartodown/                  # the package's _quartodown/, as it is
└── quartodown.scss               # theme on top of Quarto's HTML
```

The files listed under `vignettes: files:` (see [Customizing your
site](../customizing.qmd#files-the-vignettes-use)) are copied to the same paths,
so that the vignettes' relative paths to them resolve as in the package.
Documents in them aren't rendered as pages.

## The man pages

Each `man/*.Rd` file becomes a reference page, served at
`reference/<topic>.html`. It is rendered with the package's Rd macros (such as
Rdpack's `\insertRef{}`), and build-stage `\Sexpr{}` macros run with the package
installed, as in `R CMD build`. Examples run, with their output in the same
block as the code, prefixed with `#>`. To give a chunk's output a block of its
own, in a vignette too, set `#| collapse: false` on it.

To save Quarto starting an R process per page, all examples run beforehand in
one R process, which resets the global environment, search path, options and the
like between pages, as `R CMD check` does. Pages whose examples fail or produce
HTML widgets are left for Quarto to run.

Under its title, each reference page and vignette links to its source file in
the package's [repository](../customizing.qmd#the-repository), if it has one.

## Code links and tooltips

[downlit](https://downlit.r-lib.org/) links function calls in R code blocks, and
inline code like `mean()`, to their documentation. `docs/pkgdown.yml` lets
downlit on other sites link to your reference pages in turn.

That file needs the site's address: `url:` in `_quartodown/_quartodown.yml`, or
else the first `URL` in `DESCRIPTION` that isn't a GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg
repository.

References to the package's own functions also get a hover tooltip with their
usage and the first sentence of their description. `build_site()` warns when a
first sentence is longer than 200 characters, since the tooltip cuts it off. To
build without tooltips, use `build_site(tooltips = FALSE)`.

## The theme

The site has a light and a dark theme, and follows the browser's preference.
Each is built in layers:

1. the Quarto theme: `default` in light mode and `darkly` in dark mode, unless
   [`theme:`](../customizing.qmd#styling-and-layout) picks others,
2. `quartodown.scss`, quartodown's own styling,
3. `_quartodown/extra.scss`, if the package has one.

With the `default` light theme, `quartodown-fonts.scss` also gives the dark
theme the same system fonts and heading sizes.

Code output keeps the colors packages such as cli give it in a terminal, in
shades that suit the light or dark theme.
